programme.title: CloudFormation Follow Along
programme.outcome: Author declarative IaC templates using nested stacks, StackSets, custom parameters, conditions, change sets and drift detection; deploy and update the training stacks in eu-west-2; deliberately create and repair one drift event; then safely destroy only the resources created by the lab.
programme.statusNotice: Offline authoring manuscript only — not locally validated, imported, accepted, approved, published or fingerprinted.
examCoverage: CloudFormation declarative IaC and stack lifecycle
Drift creation, detection, inspection and repair
completionDefinition: Four complete YAML templates are authored from nothing.
The root stack creates fixed SSM resources and a nested child stack.
A condition is false initially and then enabled through a reviewed change set.
A self-managed StackSet deploys one instance to the current account in eu-west-2.
One root SSM parameter is deliberately changed outside CloudFormation.
Drift detection identifies RootParameter as MODIFIED.
A reviewed update repairs the drift and final drift status is IN_SYNC.
All lab resources are removed in safe reverse-dependency order.

tasks.title: Author the nested-stack template
tasks.goal: Create a complete child template that accepts parameters, creates one SSM parameter and exposes outputs to the parent.
tasks.whyItMatters: The child becomes a reusable component managed by AWS::CloudFormation::Stack.
tasks.examRelevance: Nested stacks split one deployment hierarchy into reusable template components.

browserSteps.instruction: Open C:\\cloudformation-labs\\fa-cloudformation\nested.yaml.
Replace the empty file with the complete nested.yaml block below and save it as UTF-8.
Review Environment and NestedMessage.
Confirm the fixed resource name is /fa-cloudformation/nested-message.
Review the Outputs section that the parent can read.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - open nested.yaml
cliBlocks.content: notepad .\nested.yaml

editableBlocks.title: nested.yaml
editableBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Nested stack for the fa-cloudformation SAA-C03 Follow Along.
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: training
    AllowedValues: [training, test]
  NestedMessage:
    Type: String
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 80
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$'
Resources:
  NestedParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /fa-cloudformation/nested-message
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub '${NestedMessage}-${Environment}'
      Description: Created by the nested CloudFormation stack.
      Tags:
        FollowAlong: fa-cloudformation
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation
Outputs:
  NestedParameterName:
    Value: !Ref NestedParameter
  NestedParameterArn:
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter${NestedParameter}'

expectedResults: nested.yaml contains Parameters, Resources and Outputs.

tasks.title: Author the root template with parameters and a condition
tasks.goal: Create the root template that creates a root parameter, conditionally creates another parameter and invokes the nested template by URL.
tasks.whyItMatters: One template can change behavior through runtime inputs instead of being copied for each environment.
tasks.examRelevance: Parameters make templates reusable and conditions control optional resources.

browserSteps.instruction: Open C:\\cloudformation-labs\\fa-cloudformation\root.yaml.
Paste the complete root.yaml block and save it.
Review Environment and RootMessage constraints.
Review CreateOptionalParameter and the CreateOptional condition.
Review NestedTemplateUrl; it receives the S3 URL at deployment time.
Confirm OptionalParameter has Condition: CreateOptional.
Confirm NestedTrainingStack is AWS::CloudFormation::Stack and passes two child parameters.
Review the Outputs, including !GetAtt from the child stack.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - open root.yaml
cliBlocks.content: notepad .\root.yaml

editableBlocks.title: root.yaml
editableBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Root stack for the fa-cloudformation SAA-C03 Follow Along.
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: training
    AllowedValues: [training, test]
  RootMessage:
    Type: String
    Default: created-by-fa-cloudformation
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 80
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$'
  CreateOptionalParameter:
    Type: String
    Default: 'false'
    AllowedValues: ['true', 'false']
  NestedTemplateUrl:
    Type: String
    MinLength: 20
Conditions:
  CreateOptional: !Equals [!Ref CreateOptionalParameter, 'true']
Resources:
  RootParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /fa-cloudformation/root-message
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub '${RootMessage}-${Environment}'
      Tags:
        FollowAlong: fa-cloudformation
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation
  OptionalParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Condition: CreateOptional
    Properties:
      Name: /fa-cloudformation/optional-message
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub 'optional-${Environment}'
      Tags:
        FollowAlong: fa-cloudformation
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation
  NestedTrainingStack:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
    Properties:
      TemplateURL: !Ref NestedTemplateUrl
      Parameters:
        Environment: !Ref Environment
        NestedMessage: nested-created
      TimeoutInMinutes: 10
Outputs:
  RootParameterName:
    Value: !Ref RootParameter
  OptionalParameterCreated:
    Value: !If [CreateOptional, 'true', 'false']
  NestedParameterName:
    Value: !GetAtt NestedTrainingStack.Outputs.NestedParameterName
  NestedStackId:
    Value: !Ref NestedTrainingStack

expectedResults: The nested stack receives parameters from the root.

tasks.title: Author the self-managed StackSet roles template
tasks.goal: Create the administration and execution roles declaratively in a dedicated CloudFormation template.
tasks.whyItMatters: Self-managed StackSets need a trust path from CloudFormation to the administration role and then to the execution role.
tasks.examRelevance: StackSets separate central administration from the execution identity in each target account.

browserSteps.instruction: Open C:\\cloudformation-labs\\fa-cloudformation\stackset-roles.yaml.
Paste the complete roles template and save it.
Confirm the administration role name is fa-cloudformation-stackset-admin-role.
Confirm the execution role name is fa-cloudformation-stackset-execution-role.
Confirm the administration role can assume only the exact execution role.
Confirm the execution role can manage only /fa-cloudformation/stackset-message plus DescribeParameters.
Do not add AdministratorAccess.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - open roles template
cliBlocks.content: notepad .\stackset-roles.yaml

editableBlocks.title: stackset-roles.yaml
editableBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Self-managed StackSet roles for the fa-cloudformation training lab.
Resources:
  StackSetAdministrationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: fa-cloudformation-stackset-admin-role
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: cloudformation.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: fa-cloudformation-assume-execution-role
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: sts:AssumeRole
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/fa-cloudformation-stackset-execution-role'
  StackSetExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    DependsOn: StackSetAdministrationRole
    Properties:
      RoleName: fa-cloudformation-stackset-execution-role
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !GetAtt StackSetAdministrationRole.Arn
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: fa-cloudformation-stackset-ssm-policy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: [ssm:PutParameter, ssm:GetParameter, ssm:GetParameters, ssm:DeleteParameter]
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:eu-west-2:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/fa-cloudformation/stackset-message'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ssm:DescribeParameters
                Resource: '*'
Outputs:
  AdministrationRoleArn:
    Value: !GetAtt StackSetAdministrationRole.Arn
  ExecutionRoleName:
    Value: !Ref StackSetExecutionRole

expectedResults: The template contains two named roles.
The trust chain is CloudFormation -> admin role -> execution role.
The execution policy is limited to the StackSet training parameter.

tasks.title: Author the StackSet workload template
tasks.goal: Create the template that the StackSet will deploy as a stack instance.
tasks.whyItMatters: A StackSet holds one common template while stack instances represent deployments to account/Region targets.
tasks.examRelevance: Standardized repeated deployment across accounts or Regions is a StackSet use case.

browserSteps.instruction: Open C:\\cloudformation-labs\\fa-cloudformation\stackset.yaml.
Paste the complete StackSet template and save it.

cliBlocks.content: notepad .\stackset.yaml

editableBlocks.title: stackset.yaml
editableBlocks.content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: StackSet template for the fa-cloudformation SAA-C03 Follow Along.
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: training
    AllowedValues: [training, test]
  StackSetMessage:
    Type: String
    Default: deployed-by-stackset
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 80
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$'
Resources:
  StackSetParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /fa-cloudformation/stackset-message
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub '${StackSetMessage}-${Environment}-${AWS::Region}'
      Tags:
        FollowAlong: fa-cloudformation
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation-StackSet
Outputs:
  StackSetParameterName:
    Value: !Ref StackSetParameter

expectedResults: The template contains two parameters and one SSM resource.

verificationChecks.text: No resource name escapes the training prefix.
AWS::Region is used in the value.

tasks.title: Create the root and nested stacks
tasks.goal: Deploy fa-cloudformation-root with the optional parameter disabled and confirm the nested child is created automatically.
tasks.whyItMatters: The parent owns the child lifecycle and should be used for normal create, update and delete operations.
tasks.examRelevance: Nested stacks organize reusable components inside one stack hierarchy.

browserSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation in eu-west-2 > Stacks > Create stack > With new resources.
Choose Upload a template file and select root.yaml.
Set Stack name to fa-cloudformation-root.
Set Environment=training.
Set RootMessage=created-by-fa-cloudformation.
Set CreateOptionalParameter=false.
Paste the exact NestedTemplateUrl recorded in Task 9.
Continue with default stack options and no service role.
Review and submit the stack.
Wait for CREATE_COMPLETE.
Open Resources and find NestedTrainingStack with type AWS::CloudFormation::Stack.
Open the child stack and confirm CREATE_COMPLETE.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for change set
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait change-set-create-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --change-set-name fa-cloudformation-create-root --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

tasks.title: Verify the false condition, then update through a change set
tasks.goal: Prove the initial false condition, then review and execute an update that enables the optional resource and changes RootMessage.
tasks.whyItMatters: The learner sees parameter input, condition evaluation and a change set affect real resources.
tasks.examRelevance: Change sets preview impact before updates; parameters and conditions make one template reusable.

browserSteps.instruction: Open fa-cloudformation-root > Parameters and confirm CreateOptionalParameter=false.
Open Outputs and confirm OptionalParameterCreated=false.
Open Systems Manager > Parameter Store and confirm root-message and nested-message exist while optional-message is absent.
In CloudFormation choose Stack actions > Create change set for current stack.
Use the current template.
Keep Environment=training and NestedTemplateUrl unchanged.
Change RootMessage to updated-by-fa-cloudformation.
Change CreateOptionalParameter to true.
Create the change set and wait for CREATE_COMPLETE.
Review Changes and confirm RootParameter is modified and OptionalParameter is added.
Execute the change set only after review.
Wait for UPDATE_COMPLETE.
Verify /fa-cloudformation/optional-message now exists.

tasks.title: Deploy the self-managed StackSet IAM roles
tasks.goal: Create the two StackSet roles from stackset-roles.yaml and verify the trust chain.
tasks.whyItMatters: Self-managed StackSets require administrator and execution roles even for this single-account teaching deployment.
tasks.examRelevance: StackSets use a central admin operation and an execution identity in each target account.

browserSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation > Create stack with new resources.
Upload stackset-roles.yaml.
Set Stack name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles.
Continue through the wizard.
Acknowledge creation of named IAM resources.
Create the stack and wait for CREATE_COMPLETE.
Open Outputs and record AdministrationRoleArn and ExecutionRoleName.
Open IAM > Roles and verify both fa-cloudformation StackSet roles.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create roles stack
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation create-stack --stack-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles --template-body file://stackset-roles.yaml --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for roles stack
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait stack-create-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - get admin role ARN
cliBlocks.content: $ADMIN_ROLE_ARN = aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='AdministrationRoleArn'].OutputValue | [0]" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - show admin role ARN
cliBlocks.content: Write-Output $ADMIN_ROLE_ARN

verificationChecks.text: Admin role trust principal is cloudformation.amazonaws.com.
Execution role trusts the admin role.
Execution policy is limited to the training StackSet parameter.

tasks.title: Create the StackSet and one stack instance
tasks.goal: Create fa-cloudformation-stackset with self-managed permissions and deploy one instance to the current account in eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: A single-account deployment safely teaches the same StackSet mechanism that scales across accounts and Regions.
tasks.examRelevance: Repeated standardized deployment across accounts or Regions points toward StackSets.
warnings: Do not start another StackSet operation while the current operation is RUNNING.

browserSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation > StackSets > Create StackSet.
Choose self-managed permissions.
Upload stackset.yaml.
Set StackSet name fa-cloudformation-stackset.
Use fa-cloudformation-stackset-admin-role and fa-cloudformation-stackset-execution-role.
Set Environment=training and StackSetMessage=deployed-by-stackset.
Create the StackSet.
Choose Add stacks to StackSet > Deploy new stacks.
Enter the current 12-digit account ID.
Choose eu-west-2 only.
Set failure tolerance 0 and maximum concurrent accounts 1.
Submit and wait for SUCCEEDED.
Verify /fa-cloudformation/stackset-message in Parameter Store.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild account ID
cliBlocks.content: $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID = aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-cloudformation-admin --query Account --output text

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - admin role ARN
cliBlocks.content: $ADMIN_ROLE_ARN = "arn:aws:iam::$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID:role/fa-cloudformation-stackset-admin-role"

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create StackSet
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation create-stack-set --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --template-body file://stackset.yaml --parameters ParameterKey=Environment,ParameterValue=training ParameterKey=StackSetMessage,ParameterValue=deployed-by-stackset --permission-model SELF_MANAGED --administration-role-arn $ADMIN_ROLE_ARN --execution-role-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-execution-role --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create stack instance
cliBlocks.content: $STACKSET_OPERATION_ID = aws cloudformation create-stack-instances --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --accounts $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID --regions eu-west-2 --operation-preferences FailureToleranceCount=0,MaxConcurrentCount=1 --query OperationId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect operation
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stack-set-operation --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --operation-id $STACKSET_OPERATION_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - list instances
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation list-stack-instances --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify parameter
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm get-parameter --name /fa-cloudformation/stackset-message --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

expectedResults: Exactly one stack instance targets the current account/eu-west-2.

verificationChecks.text: Stack instance is CURRENT after success.

tasks.title: Create one deliberate out-of-band change
tasks.goal: Change root-message outside CloudFormation so actual state no longer matches expected state.
tasks.whyItMatters: This creates a harmless example of unmanaged configuration change.
tasks.examRelevance: Drift detection is used to find changes made outside the IaC control plane.

browserSteps.instruction: Open Systems Manager > Parameter Store in eu-west-2.
Open /fa-cloudformation/root-message.
Choose Edit.
Set the value to DRIFTED-OUTSIDE-CLOUDFORMATION.
Save it.
Do not edit any other lab parameter.
Return to CloudFormation without updating the stack.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create deliberate drift
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm put-parameter --name /fa-cloudformation/root-message --type String --value DRIFTED-OUTSIDE-CLOUDFORMATION --overwrite --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify actual value
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm get-parameter --name /fa-cloudformation/root-message --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

expectedResults: The actual SSM value is DRIFTED-OUTSIDE-CLOUDFORMATION.

tasks.title: Detect and inspect stack drift
tasks.goal: Run drift detection and identify RootParameter as MODIFIED with different expected and actual values.
tasks.whyItMatters: The learner must interpret drift results, not merely start the check.
tasks.examRelevance: A stack is DRIFTED when supported managed resources differ from expected configuration.

browserSteps.instruction: Open fa-cloudformation-root in CloudFormation.
Choose Stack actions > Detect drift.
Confirm the request and wait for completion.
Open drift results.
Confirm stack drift status DRIFTED.
Find RootParameter with resource drift status MODIFIED.
Inspect the expected value and actual DRIFTED-OUTSIDE-CLOUDFORMATION value.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - start drift detection
cliBlocks.content: $DRIFT_ID = aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --query StackDriftDetectionId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - poll drift status
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stack-drift-detection-status --stack-drift-detection-id $DRIFT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect modified resources
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stack-resource-drifts --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --stack-resource-drift-status-filters MODIFIED --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

expectedResults: Actual value shows the deliberate manual value.

verificationChecks.text: RootParameter is the deliberate drifted resource.

tasks.title: Repair drift through a reviewed CloudFormation update
tasks.goal: Change RootMessage through a reviewed change set, execute it, then confirm a new drift check is IN_SYNC.
tasks.whyItMatters: The repair restores CloudFormation as the source of truth instead of accepting the manual edit.
tasks.examRelevance: A controlled CloudFormation update should bring managed state back in line and then be verified.

browserSteps.instruction: Open fa-cloudformation-root > Stack actions > Create change set for current stack.
Use the current template.
Keep Environment=training, CreateOptionalParameter=true and NestedTemplateUrl unchanged.
Set RootMessage=repaired-by-fa-cloudformation.
Create and wait for the change set.
Confirm RootParameter is the intended modification.
Execute and wait for UPDATE_COMPLETE.
Run Detect drift again.
Wait for the new detection to finish.
Confirm stack drift status IN_SYNC.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create repair change set
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --change-set-name fa-cloudformation-repair-drift --change-set-type UPDATE --use-previous-template --parameters ParameterKey=Environment,UsePreviousValue=true ParameterKey=RootMessage,ParameterValue=repaired-by-fa-cloudformation ParameterKey=CreateOptionalParameter,UsePreviousValue=true ParameterKey=NestedTemplateUrl,UsePreviousValue=true --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for repair change set
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait change-set-create-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --change-set-name fa-cloudformation-repair-drift --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect repair
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-change-set --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --change-set-name fa-cloudformation-repair-drift --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - execute repair
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation execute-change-set --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --change-set-name fa-cloudformation-repair-drift --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for repair
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait stack-update-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify repaired value
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm get-parameter --name /fa-cloudformation/root-message --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - start second drift
cliBlocks.content: $DRIFT_ID_2 = aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --query StackDriftDetectionId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - poll second drift
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stack-drift-detection-status --stack-drift-detection-id $DRIFT_ID_2 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

verificationChecks.text: The repair change set was reviewed first.
Final root stack drift status is IN_SYNC.

tasks.title: Review SAA-C03 CloudFormation decision points
tasks.goal: Turn the practical work into clear architecture decision rules before teardown.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam rewards recognizing the correct CloudFormation mechanism from a requirement.
tasks.examRelevance: CloudFormation is explicitly in scope for SAA-C03.

browserSteps.instruction: Template means declarative desired state.
Stack means one managed collection of resources.
Parameter means runtime input without editing the template.
Condition means true/false logic controlling resource or output creation.
Nested stack means a child AWS::CloudFormation::Stack inside a parent hierarchy.
StackSet means centrally distributing one template to target accounts/Regions.
Change set means previewing proposed stack changes before execution.
Drift means actual managed state differs from expected template state.
Exam trigger: repeated standardized deployment across accounts/Regions -> StackSets.
Exam trigger: reusable components inside one deployment hierarchy -> nested stacks.
Exam trigger: manual out-of-band changes -> drift detection.
Exam trigger: preview stack impact before update -> change set.
Exam trap: nested stacks and StackSets solve different problems.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - final root inventory
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - final StackSet inventory
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation list-stack-instances --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - final parameter inventory
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/fa-cloudformation/" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

expectedResults: The learner can explain stack vs nested stack vs StackSet.
The learner can explain parameter vs condition.
The learner can explain change set vs drift detection.

verificationChecks.text: Root stack is IN_SYNC before cleanup.

tasks.title: Delete every CloudFormation training resource in reverse dependency order
tasks.goal: Remove the StackSet instance first, then StackSet, root/nested stacks, role stack, S3 artifacts, temporary identity and local files.
tasks.whyItMatters: Deleting credentials or templates too early can strand managed resources, so cleanup preserves dependencies until they are no longer needed.
tasks.examRelevance: Delete through the owning CloudFormation control plane rather than manually deleting child resources first.
warnings: If the StackSet delete operation is still RUNNING, wait for SUCCEEDED before deleting the StackSet or roles.

browserSteps.instruction: Open CloudFormation > StackSets and open fa-cloudformation-stackset.
Delete the stack instance for the current account in eu-west-2 and choose not to retain the stack.
Wait until the delete operation succeeds.
Delete the now-empty fa-cloudformation-stackset.
Open CloudFormation > Stacks.
Delete fa-cloudformation-root and wait for it to disappear; do not delete the nested child directly.
Open Systems Manager Parameter Store and verify root-message, optional-message and nested-message are absent.
Delete fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles and wait for it to disappear.
Open IAM Roles and verify both fa-cloudformation StackSet roles are absent.
Open the exact S3 template bucket from Task 3.
Delete nested.yaml, then delete the empty bucket.
Verify /fa-cloudformation/stackset-message is absent.
Sign in as root only now: delete the fa-cloudformation-admin access key, detach/delete fa-cloudformation-admin-policy, delete fa-cloudformation-admin, then sign out of root.
Remove only the fa-cloudformation-admin AWS CLI profile; leave unrelated profiles unchanged.
Delete C:\cloudformation-labs\fa-cloudformation last.
Read and affirm the programme cleanup acknowledgement.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild account ID
cliBlocks.content: $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID = aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-cloudformation-admin --query Account --output text

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete StackSet instance
cliBlocks.content: $DELETE_OPERATION_ID = aws cloudformation delete-stack-instances --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --accounts $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID --regions eu-west-2 --no-retain-stacks --query OperationId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - inspect delete operation
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation describe-stack-set-operation --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --operation-id $DELETE_OPERATION_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete empty StackSet
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation delete-stack-set --stack-set-name fa-cloudformation-stackset --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete root stack
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait root delete
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-root --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify SSM absence
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm describe-parameters --parameter-filters "Key=Name,Option=BeginsWith,Values=/fa-cloudformation/" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete role stack
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait role stack delete
cliBlocks.content: aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --stack-name fa-cloudformation-stackset-roles --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild bucket
cliBlocks.content: $TEMPLATE_BUCKET = "fa-cloudformation-$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID-templates"

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete nested object
cliBlocks.content: aws s3 rm "s3://$TEMPLATE_BUCKET/nested.yaml" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete bucket
cliBlocks.content: aws s3api delete-bucket --bucket $TEMPLATE_BUCKET --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudformation-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - leave lab folder
cliBlocks.content: Set-Location C:\

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete local lab folder
cliBlocks.content: Remove-Item "C:\cloudformation-labs\fa-cloudformation" -Recurse -Force

expectedResults: StackSet instance and StackSet are gone.
Root stack and nested child are gone.
StackSet roles stack and both roles are gone.
nested.yaml and template bucket are gone.
Temporary IAM user, access key, policy and CLI profile are removed.
Local lab directory is removed last.

verificationChecks.text: Unrelated resources and CLI profiles remain unchanged.

troubleshooting.title: Template validation fails
troubleshooting.likelyCause: YAML indentation, quoting or copied content changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the local file with the complete editable block and correct the first validation error before deployment.

troubleshooting.title: Nested stack cannot read TemplateURL
troubleshooting.likelyCause: nested.yaml is missing, URL is wrong, or S3 read permission is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Rebuild TEMPLATE_BUCKET/NESTED_URL from the verified account ID and confirm nested.yaml exists in that private bucket.

troubleshooting.title: Root stack rolls back
troubleshooting.likelyCause: A nested resource failed, an exact SSM name already exists, or a parameter constraint failed.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Events, find the first CREATE_FAILED event and follow the nested stack link when NestedTrainingStack failed.

troubleshooting.title: OptionalParameter is not in the change set
troubleshooting.likelyCause: CreateOptionalParameter was not changed to true.
troubleshooting.fix: Recreate the change set with CreateOptionalParameter=true and keep NestedTemplateUrl unchanged.

troubleshooting.title: StackSet cannot pass the administration role
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The roles stack is not complete or the training user lacks the exact restricted iam:PassRole permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify the roles stack is CREATE_COMPLETE and the admin role ARN exactly matches fa-cloudformation-stackset-admin-role.

troubleshooting.title: StackSet instance operation fails
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Role trust/permissions are wrong or stackset-message already exists.
troubleshooting.fix: Inspect describe-stack-set-operation and list-stack-set-operation-results, then verify both roles and the exact SSM name.

troubleshooting.title: Drift remains IN_SYNC after manual edit
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The wrong SSM parameter was edited or the new value was not saved.
troubleshooting.fix: Read /fa-cloudformation/root-message directly and confirm DRIFTED-OUTSIDE-CLOUDFORMATION before rerunning drift detection.

troubleshooting.title: Final drift check remains DRIFTED
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Another resource changed manually or the repair update did not complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Describe all resource drifts and repair only the lab resource whose actual state differs from the template.

troubleshooting.title: StackSet cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: A stack instance still exists or the instance deletion is still running.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the delete operation to reach SUCCEEDED and confirm the instance list is empty before deleting the StackSet.

troubleshooting.title: S3 bucket cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.fix: List the exact bucket, delete nested.yaml only, then retry deleting the bucket.
